We employed a two-tier human-in-the-loop verification process. This approach combines document-level recall checks with native-speaker scrutiny of L1 interference claims, providing a principled estimate of annotation quality.

Two native-speaker linguists (Arabic and Mandarin) independently evaluated 10 randomly-selected errors per language flagged as L1 interference by GPT-4. They answered the following questions: -Q1 (Plausibility): Is this a plausible case of L1 interference? (Yes / No + rationale). -Q2 (Explanation): Is GPT-4's explanation of the interference accurate? (Yes / No + rationale).
guideline: Evaluators assessed plausibility of L1 interference, accuracy of explanations, error detection, correction agreement, type agreement, and L1 reason agreement.
